target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session or `/reset`.

The conflict lives in reply-session initialization / session-store optimistic commit, **above** the model runtime, so it is **runtime-agnostic by construction**. Every case we observed live ran under the Codex app-server harness; on that harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is a runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover — not anything Codex-specific.

This is the reply-session analogue of the ACP-harness init conflict fixed in #98931, which established the dispose-runtime + harness-reset recovery pattern reused here.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: dispose the wedged runtime + run harness self-heal, then retry init exactly once (recursion bounded by `conflictRecoveryAttempted`)
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

**Safety fence (commit `ede72284b`):** the first version of the self-heal called the teardown primitives inline while holding `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`. That lock does not block a foreign turn's execution, so a genuinely active concurrent turn on the same sessionKey (hot topic / rapid messages / rollover racing a fresh turn) could be disposed mid-flight, and draining inside the lock could deadlock. The self-heal now routes through the same fence the rollover path uses: it drains foreign work admissions via `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` **outside** the store-write lock before disposing the wedged runtime and retrying. No new machinery — it reuses `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions`.

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Evidence
**Focused tests**
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → **142/142 pass** (4 decider unit tests + 138 session tests, including 2 new integration tests driving the real `session.ts` wiring: a forced double commit conflict disposes the wedged MCP runtime and completes in exactly 3 commit attempts; an actively-admitted foreign turn is interrupted/drained before teardown rather than torn down).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`).

**Live proof.** Captured on a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 host. The wedge reproduced on **two independent agents / sessionKeys**, each re-hitting the identical conflict on the same persistent sessionKey for the same inbound message across repeated retries — a permanent wedge, not a transient race. Group/topic identifiers redacted; structure and error text preserved.

```
# Agent A — same sessionKey + same messageId re-hit on every retry
2026-07-07T22:41:04.633Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:41:10.189Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted ..."
2026-07-07T22:41:20.687Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:41:41.222Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:42:21.772Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error

# Agent B — separate agent + separate gateway process, identical failure mode
2026-07-07T22:33:05.485Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:33:10.578Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:34:21.172Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
```

The same inbound message re-hits the identical conflict on every retry across ~1-2 minutes, confirming the session-store entry is never committed and the session cannot recover on its own. Operational mitigation before this fix was `/reset` or a fresh session.

## Scope
This addresses the conflict-wedge failure mode. It does not attempt to address a separate operational failure where the Codex app-server child is not running at all — a different cause that presents the same empty-tool-result surface.
